name: capture_bulb_image_region
description: captureBulbImage ARM code region: the function that owns the message-driven stop edge and calls capture_image_with_Bulb. The binary is proprietary Benro firmware, never committed, supplied locally (see capture_bulb_image_region.bin.placeholder). This sidecar records only coordinates and hashes - no firmware content.

provenance.layout_note: Same constraint as stage2_region: the function resolves globals with ldr rN,[pc,#imm] + add rN,pc,rN, so it must load at its original vaddr. code_address/code_size map a page-aligned range covering the blob and its referenced globals (.rodata 0x25cfb0/0x25d070, .dynamic 0x2f6ffc).
provenance.stub_entries_note: All 17 BL sites resolved from the retained source ELF: 9 via .symtab FUNC entries and 8 via .rel.plt -> .dynsym. model is call-site because the intercepted address is the BL inside the mapped blob.
provenance.boundary_aliases_note: The lifecycle cases assert on an idealised vocabulary. In this binary the message-driven stop edge is implemented by stopCaptureImageForMessage (0x202e4), called from captureBulbImage at 0x207e8. context_cancel has no counterpart here; gp_context_cancel (0x358d0) is libgphoto-internal with 27 call sites, none in this function.

observed_behaviour.interpretation: Execution reaches 10 real boundary calls including capture_image_with_Bulb, then faults at 0x20750 on ldr r3,[r3]: the preceding ldr r3,[r4,r3] loads a .rodata string address (e.g. 0x25cfb0) and the code dereferences it as a pointer, which only makes sense with the real global contents and a populated caller frame. stopCaptureImageForMessage at 0x207e8 lies beyond that fault, so the stop edge is present in this region but not yet reachable by straight-line execution.
observed_behaviour.reachability_gap: Reaching 0x207e8 needs (a) the referenced .rodata/.data words mapped with their real contents and (b) AAPCS argument setup for captureBulbImage's parameters. Neither is in scope for this fixture; both are recorded here so the gap is explicit rather than silently green.
